title: Decommission v0 admin shims and unify deployment manifests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last three years we accumulated a set of v0 admin shims and backwards‑compat endpoints that were added to support early rollout flows and customer integrations. These shims complicate routing logic, lead to duplicated rollout manifests, and increase the surface area for bugs in the runtime. Several recent incidents (see INCIDENT-2024-11-rollout-conflict) showed these code paths are tested less frequently and cause inconsistent behavior across Dedicated and Private installs.

Goal: Remove the v0 admin compatibility layer (HTTP shims and v0 query param routing), migrate users/automation to the canonical v1 manifest APIs, and consolidate per-tenant rollout manifests into a single versioned manifest format. The outcome should be: simpler routing code, one canonical manifest format for rollouts, fewer feature-flag code paths, and no customer-visible regressions.

Scope:
- Delete the runtime compat proxy and v0 admin endpoints under /admin/v0/* after migration.
- Migrate stored rollout metadata in DB table rollout_manifests_v0 -> rollout_manifests (canonicalized); provide a migration job with dry-run and verification.
- Replace legacy toggle read paths that read flags from both new and legacy columns (remove duplicate reads).
- Remove the runtime config switch EDUCATE_LEGACY_CLIENTS and associated feature flags.
- Update API docs & console links to point at the unified manifest editor.

Out of scope: Full rewrite of rollout engine. We will not change rollout semantics beyond format/field renames; behavior remains identical unless explicitly noted.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Audit: Create an export of active v0 manifests and callers (admin scripts, automation, customers) — Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/389203/v0-manifest-audit.
2) Migration shim: Add a one‑time migration job (idempotent) that reads v0 rows, canonicalizes fields (map: old_routes -> route_manifest.routes, old_version -> manifest_version 1), writes to rollout_manifests with a migration tag, and marks the v0 row as migrated. Dry-run mode writes to a migration-preview table and emits a CSV report.
3) Compatibility wrapper: For two cycles, keep a read-only compatibility wrapper that translates v0 reads into the new format inside the control plane; log counts and customers using it.
4) Remove write paths that still emit v0 manifests (console, API clients). Update console save logic and ensure SDKs use the canonical route.
5) Validation: Run end-to-end tests that exercise canary rollouts, A/B, and fallback policy. Use the internal eval harness to run synthetic requests and confirm rollout routing parity.
6) Deployment & rollout: Release migration job to staging, run dry-run, validate, then run to production in low-traffic window. Monitor error budgets and routing mismatch metrics for 72 hours.
7) Deletion: After 2 cycles (minimum 30 days) with zero critical mismatches and sign-off from PM and SRE, remove compat proxy code and drop v0 tables/columns.

Acceptance criteria:
- All active rollout manifests are present in rollout_manifests in canonical format and flagged as migrated.
- No production services depend on /admin/v0 endpoints (0 hits over 7 days).
- Console and SDKs have no write paths that produce v0 manifests (verified via unit tests and integration smoke tests).
- Migration is idempotent and reversible for the first 48 hours (soft-rollback via re-inserting v0 rows).
- Post-migration routing parity: <0.1% routing mismatches across synthetic tests and production telemetry for 72h.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for canonicalizer mapping (field-by-field asserts).
- Integration tests: staging migration run + smoke deploy, exercise canary/A/B flows.
- E2E: synthetic traffic using internal harness with golden manifests; compare decisions before/after migration.
- Load: run migration job against a copy of prod DB (privacy-sanitized) to measure runtime/IO.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: Customers or automation still calling v0 endpoints. Mitigation: communication plan (email + Console banner), compatibility wrapper for 2 cycles, 301 redirects for GETs during the window.
- Risk: Migration job causes DB load. Mitigation: batch writes, rate-limited runner, and online index creation where possible.
- Risk: Hidden fields in v0 not mapped correctly. Mitigation: preflight dry-run with sampling, manual review of discrepancies, and owner sign-off.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (staging): collect audit -> run dry-run migration -> fix canonicalizer.
- Week 2 (canary): run migration in prod for 5% tenant subset (non-critical), monitor metrics/dashboards: rollout-routing-mismatch, admin-endpoint-traffic, migration-errors.
- Week 3 (full): run migration to 100% in a low-traffic window. Keep compatibility wrapper.
- Week 6+: if stable, merge removal PR for compat proxy and schedule DB schema cleanup in maintenance window.

Artifacts & links:
- Audit doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/389203/v0-manifest-audit
- Migration branch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4273
- Migration runner (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/tree/main/migrations/manifest-migrator
- Dashboard (staging/prod): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollout-migration/manifest-migration-overview

- SRE lead: David Kim
- Console/UX: Priya Shah

Security review required: true

Done criteria:
- Compat proxy code removed and merged.
- rollout_manifests_v0 table dropped or archived to cold storage.
- Console user journeys, SDKs, and internal automation updated with tests.
- Post-cleanup playbook and incident runbook updated and linked from the ticket.
